open_points.subject: json_depth measurement mechanism
open_points.text: `json_depth_max` bounds each JSON text where it enters the kernel, measured on that text as a whole, without recursion, before anything else walks it
open_points.question: Which module owns the non-recursive depth-measurement mechanism used by `surface`, `canonical_values`, `sandbox`/`sandbox_runner`, `service_invoker`, `installation`, `bindings` and `run_values`, and through which allowed capability do the consumers use it?
options: `canonical_values` owns one raw-JSON depth capability and the dependency list is adjusted
Each entry-point module implements and owns its own depth scanner
`data_provider` owns executable depth checking in addition to the constant
open_points.default_guess: Give `canonical_values` one depth-measurement capability and make every raw-JSON consumer that needs it an allowed dependency.

open_points.subject: function value output representation
open_points.text: `run` ... returning a dict ... A `value` port carries the JSON value decoded to Python ... The output count is the sum of the canonical JSON bytes of every `value` output — for an output that has none, the bytes of its JSON text as returned
open_points.question: What is the "JSON text as returned" when agent code returns a Python object rather than JSON text, and which module creates and preserves those bytes so depth and output size can be checked before another walk or serialization fails?
options: The runner serializes each returned Python value once and reports those exact bytes
The parent serializes the decoded runner value and counts that serialization
A value with no canonical bytes has no countable text and is immediately a contract violation
open_points.default_guess: Have `sandbox_runner` serialize each returned value once with a bounded non-recursive encoder and report the exact bytes to `sandbox`.

open_points.subject: mapped-list failure under changing json_depth_max
open_points.text: No record of the node states that failure: like the list, it is derived from the elements' records and those two ceilings, the same way by every reader of the trace ... A new release may change ceilings ... recorded executions are never reinterpreted.
open_points.question: Which release's `json_depth_max` must readers use when deriving an unrecorded mapped-list failure after the configured ceiling has changed, and where is that governing value or release recorded?
options: Use the ceiling in force when the list first entered the kernel and persist enough provenance to recover it
Use the reader's current release ceiling, allowing the derived historical result to change
open_points.default_guess: Use and persist the ceiling in force when the list was first assembled for delivery.

open_points.subject: old deep stored values returned by functions
open_points.text: each value output of a function, as its own text ... A deeper text is ... refused where it enters ... every record stored under an earlier release — its values, constants and schemas — is read, executed with and returned as before
open_points.question: After `json_depth_max` is lowered, is a function output equal to an older stored value deeper than the new limit a newly entering text that must fail, or an older value that must be returned as before?
options: Every function output is new input to the kernel and is checked against the current ceiling
An output equal to an existing StoredValue is exempt from remeasurement
The preservation promise covers inspection/direct delivery only, not newly produced function outputs
open_points.default_guess: Treat every function output as newly entering and interpret “returned as before” as applying only to direct reads and delivery of existing records.
